first_impression.reaction: Neither of us wants to stand up and do a five-minute speech in front of James's colleagues, so 'say something true, say it well and hand the moment back' is exactly us. The intro also says it covers what Australian law makes us say, which I actually want to know. No 'dream day' nonsense. I'll keep going.

journey.quote: Many would rather say something true, say it well and hand the moment back to the ceremony.
journey.reaction: That's us. Calm, grown-up tone, not gushing. Good start.

journey.section: How long should short wedding vows be?
journey.quote: Our advice is to keep vows to 1 to 2 minutes each.
journey.reaction: The headline says under one minute, then the advice is 1 to 2 minutes. Not a big deal, but I had to read it twice to work out which one you actually recommend.

journey.section: How long should short wedding vows be?
journey.quote: Then ask your partner to do the same so the two of you land at a similar length.
journey.reaction: Practical. James would write three lines and I'd write a page, so this one will save an argument.

journey.section: What words do you legally have to say when you marry in Australia?
journey.quote: When your celebrant is not a minister of religion, it is sufficient for each of you to say to the other, in the presence of the celebrant and the witnesses, the words set out in section 45(2) of the Marriage Act 1961:
journey.reaction: Linked to the actual Act, with the section number. As a lawyer I appreciate that nobody is paraphrasing the legal bit. This is the 'legal side sorted' feeling I want.

journey.quote: If you marry legally in another country, the legal wording follows that country.
journey.reaction: Fine, but this is the part that matters most to us and it's two sentences and one New Zealand example. Do people usually do the legal bit in Sydney and a ceremony overseas? Is an overseas marriage recognised back home? That's my real question and it isn't here.

journey.quote: Your celebrant or registrar sets the words; the place, the guests and the travel are the bigger puzzle.
journey.reaction: True, and at least this plug is sitting next to the overseas section rather than in the middle of a list. It reads naturally.

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: 'One Wedded Advisor' and 'single point of contact' are what we want. 'Anywhere in the world' is the line every planner uses though. Who actually finds us a celebrant or registrar overseas?

journey.quote: Not only today, with everyone dressed up and the light just right, but the Tuesday nights, the airport queues and the years our hair turns grey.
journey.reaction: This one I'd actually steal. Specific and not soppy. Our friends wouldn't cringe.

journey.quote: I will listen. I will laugh with you, often. And I will show up every day, especially the hard ones.
journey.reaction: Short and doesn't try too hard. James's style exactly.
That one's a bit Instagram caption. The funny section mostly works but this line tips into try-hard.

journey.quote: Thank you to everyone who crossed oceans to be here.
journey.reaction: Half our guests will be flying in, so this is a nice touch. I'd use a version of this.

journey.quote: I will be your compass and your companion.
journey.reaction: Compass is a bit greeting card. Number 17 is better than 18.

journey.section: How do you say your vows with confidence?
journey.quote: Wind, waves and fountains swallow voices.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of thing you only know if you've been to a lot of outdoor weddings. My grandparents would hear nothing at a clifftop ceremony without a mic.

journey.section: How do you say your vows with confidence?
journey.quote: Ask your venue whether a microphone is available for the ceremony, who sets it up, and whether you can test it at the rehearsal.
journey.reaction: Good question, but again it's handed back to us. If we're paying a planner, isn't that the Advisor's job to check?

journey.quote: Our advice is 1 to 2 minutes each. Every example in this guide runs well under a minute, so read yours aloud and time it before the day.
journey.reaction: The FAQ mostly repeats what I just read. Skimmed it.

unanswered_questions: If we marry overseas, is the marriage recognised in Australia, or should we do the legal part in Sydney first and have the ceremony abroad?
Does a Wedded Advisor find and book the celebrant or registrar overseas, and brief them on our own vows? (deferred business detail)
Does the Advisor confirm ceremony sound (microphone, who sets it up) with the venue, or is that on us? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real wedding (venue, date) showing a destination ceremony with personal vows? (deferred business detail)
Which countries besides New Zealand let couples write their own vows around the legal words?

turn_offs_found.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Anywhere in the world' is the generic end-to-end claim every planner makes. It doesn't say anything specific about ceremonies, celebrants or legal paperwork, which is what this page is about.
Slightly cliché, caption-style line. Minor, but it's the kind of thing our friends would smirk at.

would_share_with: James: examples 6 and 8 and the 'time it aloud' tip, so we agree on a length before either of us starts writing
My parents: probably not the vows. Maybe Dad, for the legal section, since he'll ask whether an overseas wedding 'counts'

cta_reaction.quote: The words are yours to write. Where you say them, and who flies in to hear them, is where a Wedded Advisor comes in.
cta_reaction.why: It's a nice, low-key close and not pushy, which I like. But a vows article isn't why we'd hire a planner, there's no real wedding or price range here, and it doesn't answer whether we should marry legally at home or abroad. I'd bookmark it and send it to James, not enquire yet.

top_3_changes: Expand 'Marrying overseas' beyond one sentence and a New Zealand example. Tell us whether couples usually marry legally in Australia and hold the ceremony abroad, and whether an overseas marriage is recognised here.
Make the Concierge line specific to ceremonies: say whether the Wedded Advisor finds the celebrant or registrar abroad and checks things like the microphone, instead of 'anywhere in the world'.
Line up the length message: the title says 'under one minute' but the advice says 'keep vows to 1 to 2 minutes each'. Say which you recommend and why.
